summary: Finite-depth unipotent Albanese maps, represented crystalline periods and global Selmer localization give image-defined and Zariski-closure Chabauty–Kim loci. nodes.title: The period of an admissible path torsor
nodes.statement: Let K be a characteristic-zero p-adic field and U_n the finite-depth de Rham unipotent group of NC.2. Write H_n=F⁰U_n, a closed split unipotent subgroup, not assumed normal, and Q_n=U_n/H_n for the represented quotient by right multiplication. On a commutative K-algebra R, an admissible right U_n-torsor T has the NC.2 finite coordinate filtration, a compatible Frobenius with a unique fixed point p_φ, and a Hodge reduction F⁰T with an R-point p_H. Define admissiblePeriod(T)=[u] in Q_n(R), where p_φ·u=p_H. Changing p_H to p_H·h changes u to uh for h∈H_n(R), hence preserves its class. Quotient representability and triviality of split-unipotent torsors over affine bases are imported inputs. Native point reduction: for a Torsor U_nᵒᵖ T, u is the underlying U_n element of p_H divided by p_φ in the opposite group; the point quotient is Mathlib's left-coset carrier U_n/H_n with relation u⁻¹v∈H_n.
hypotheses: U_n and its filtered/Frobenius path structure come from NC.2; Frobenius Lang invertibility uses the positive-weight hypotheses there, not an arbitrary automorphism of an arbitrary unipotent group.
All R are commutative K-algebras, including nonreduced ones; H_n is smooth split unipotent and the Hodge torsor is trivial over Spec R.
proofSteps: Use the imported homogeneous quotient sheaf and its affine representation; the affine torsor-vanishing input identifies Q_n(R) with right-multiplication orbits U_n(R)/H_n(R).

Use the NC.2 Frobenius Lang scheme isomorphism after coefficient extension to obtain the unique fixed section on every affine coefficient algebra; identify T(R) with U_n(R), retaining the right-action order. The field-endpoint canonical-path theorem alone does not supply this all-algebra step.
Hodge points differ by right multiplication by H_n; quotient this difference.
acceptance: No group structure on Q_n is asserted when H_n is nonnormal.
For the neutral filtered Frobenius torsor with p_H=p_φ, the period is [1].

nodes.title: Admissible torsors and the Hodge quotient
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of admissible-period, the period gives a natural bijection, for every commutative K-algebra R, between isomorphism classes of admissible U_n-torsors and Q_n(R). Isomorphisms preserve the right torsor action, coordinate filtration, Frobenius and Hodge filtration. This represents the finite-level admissible-torsor functor, rather than merely classifying K-points. The Hodge structure is the full NC.2 normalized multiplicative filtration; a reduction to H_n without that structure is not silently substituted for it.
hypotheses: Admissibility, split-unipotent affine torsor vanishing and normalized filtered structure as in admissible-period.
proofSteps: An isomorphism preserves p_φ by its uniqueness and maps Hodge points to Hodge points, so periods agree.
For equal cosets, the unique p_φ-compatible torsor isomorphism differs in Hodge coordinates by an element of H_n, and preserves the normalized filtration.
For g∈U_n(R), use the standard filtered torsor U_n,R with Frobenius φ_g(h)=g⁻¹φ(gh); its fixed point is g⁻¹ and its Hodge point 1, giving period [g].
Apply the finite central quotient to Kim Proposition 1 and verify scalar-extension naturality.
acceptance: The twisted Frobenius satisfies φ_g(hk)=φ_g(h)φ(k); it is generally not a group homomorphism.
The construction works on R=K[ε]/(ε²), not just reduced points.

nodes.title: The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map
nodes.statement: Fix a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve X/K, a smooth proper O_K-model X̄ with finite étale boundary D (possibly empty), the open model 𝒳=X̄∖D and b∈𝒳(O_K). Use U_n=U/Γ_{n+1} for n≥1 and the right path torsor P_n(b,x) from b to x. Define localAlbanese_n:𝒳(O_K)→Q_n(K) by x↦admissiblePeriod(P_n(b,x)). The map is a p-adic analytic map on each residue disc, with local coordinates furnished by iterated Coleman integrals and an algebraic Hodge trivialization. It is not asserted to be a morphism of algebraic K-schemes. At b it equals [1]. Kim's U_{n+1} is this U_n; Kim U_1 is trivial and Kim U_2 is our depth one.
hypotheses: The base point is integral and the compactification and boundary have good reduction at the chosen p-adic place.
NC.2 supplies the canonical Frobenius path and normalized Hodge reduction.

For an arbitrary ramified K/ℚ_p, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The cited NC.2 berthelot-ogus and crystalline-path-coordinates nodes cover unramified models; finite-path-comparison extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. General ramified-model comparison is requested explicitly, not inferred from coefficient extension.
proofSteps: Push the NC.2 tensor path family to the n-th central quotient.
Apply admissible-classification fibrewise, independent of the chosen local Hodge section.
Use the word-path comparison of NC.2 and Coleman local expansions for discwise analyticity.
acceptance: The depth-zero extension is the constant map to a point; depth one is nontrivial.
The base point maps to the neutral coset and higher-depth maps project to lower-depth maps.

nodes.title: Iterated integrals as Albanese coordinates
nodes.statement: On an affine open of X_K choose the NC.2 universal connection and its algebraic trivialization g, and choose an algebraic Hodge trivialization p_H=gγ. Let p_φ(x)u(x)=g(x). Then localAlbanese_n(x) is the class of u(x)γ(x) in Q_n. In the NC.2 affine trivialization the Frobenius path has word element I(b,x), while g has coordinate 1; hence u=I(b,x)⁻¹ and the period representative is I(b,x)⁻¹γ(x). The coefficients of I are the imported Coleman iterated integrals; coefficients of I⁻¹ are their antipode combinations. Kim’s variable u in his proof must not be identified with NC.2’s forward path element without transporting the trivialization convention. In the convention dI_{iw}=ω_i I_w, the first letter is the outermost integration, I_∅=1, and the coefficients of uγ are ∑_{w=ab}(I⁻¹)_aγ_b, preserving multiplication order. On proper curves use the imported maximal extending quotient of an affine universal connection; do not treat all affine words as independent coordinates on the proper group. Regular functions on Q_n pull back to Coleman functions, analytic on every ordinary residue disc.
hypotheses: Good-reduction datum of local-albanese; the affine trivializations and word-path identification are the NC.2 imported constructions.
Only ordinary discs of 𝒳 are evaluated; logarithmic boundary germs are not added to the integral-point domain.
proofSteps: Use the ordered torsor equation p_φuγ=p_H and the existing shuffle/deconcatenation word realization.
The Hodge factor γ is algebraic, so finite polynomial coordinate expressions are Coleman functions.
Pass from the affine group to the central quotient and to the proper extending quotient when required.
acceptance: A bare list of single integrals cannot encode depth two.
The empty coefficient is 1, and reversing factors u and γ changes noncommuting coordinates.

nodes.title: Kim density on every residue disc
nodes.statement: For local-albanese's smooth hyperbolic good-reduction pair over a finite extension K/ℚ_p, n≥1, and every nonempty integral residue disc B⊆𝒳(O_K), the image localAlbanese_n(B) is Zariski dense in the geometrically integral affine K-variety Q_n. Equivalently any regular f∈O(Q_n) that vanishes on this whole disc is zero. The conclusion is K-Zariski density, not automatic ℚ_p-Zariski density in Res_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n. Density is asserted separately on each disc, so a nonzero regular equation has nonzero analytic pullback on every disc.
hypotheses: All good-reduction and integrality hypotheses of local-albanese.
n≥1 in our indexing, corresponding to Kim n+1≥2; hyperbolicity means 2g−2+deg D>0.
proofSteps: Kim Lemma 4 proves the affine forward horizontal word coefficients independent over algebraic functions via complex monodromy and induction on word length.

For the group-like shuffle series, inversion sends a length-r word coefficient to (−1)^r times the reversed-word coefficient. Thus the inverse coefficients retain this independence. Right multiplication by the algebraic Hodge factor γ is unitriangular in word length, with γ_empty=1. Hence the corrected representative I⁻¹γ is dense in the affine group and its image in Q_n is dense.

Use the surjective proper extending quotient to pass from an auxiliary affine curve to the proper curve. Choose a finite étale boundary divisor avoiding the chosen disc; it need not be a K-rational point in a different disc. This repairs the unsupported point choice on Kim p.111 (E-NC4-4), and its integral chart interface is requested from L1.

On another nonempty disc choose an integral lift c. Canonical path composition gives I(b,x)=I(c,x)I(b,c); multiplication by the constant group-like factor, inversion and the algebraic Hodge correction preserve the triangular independence argument. This proves density for the original base point on every disc, rather than inferring it merely from global density.
acceptance: At our depth one the image in Lie(J) is dense even if the local curve has analytic dimension one and g>1.
The ℚ_p-Weil restriction dimension cannot replace dim_K Q_n in a single-place argument without a stronger density/nonvanishing input.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, p.93; §1 proof and Lemma 4, pp.111–114; §3, p.121
sources.match: Kim proves density already on a residue disc and then applies the nonvanishing consequence on every disc in the finiteness argument.

nodes.title: The represented crystalline period map
nodes.statement: Let K/ℚ_p be finite and let L_n=H¹_f(G_K,U_n^et) be the represented finite-depth crystalline torsor functor of NC.3. The NC.2 filtered, Frobenius and multiplicative period comparisons send a crystalline torsor T over a ℚ_p-algebra R to an admissible de Rham U_n-torsor over K⊗_{ℚ_p}R. Compose with admissible-classification to obtain a natural transformation D_n(R):L_n(R)→Q_n(K⊗R), and hence a morphism of ℚ_p-schemes crystallinePeriodMap_n:L_n→Res_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n. On ℚ_p-points the target is Q_n(K). The neutral torsor maps to [1]. No inverse of D_n is asserted. Native affine reduction takes the resulting pullback d*:O(Res Q_n)→O(L_n) and sends an R-point c to c∘d*; deriving d* from crystalline torsors remains part of the nonlinear supplier interface.
hypotheses: Representability over all ℚ_p-algebras and coefficient-compatible crystalline conditions, as in NC.3.
The nonlinear comparison respects multiplication, both path augmentations, torsor coactions, Hodge filtration and Frobenius; linear H¹ comparison alone is insufficient.
For K≠ℚ_p the represented target is the Weil restriction, not Q_n as a ℚ_p-scheme by omission of its field.

For an arbitrary ramified K/ℚ_p, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The cited NC.2 berthelot-ogus and crystalline-path-coordinates nodes cover unramified models; finite-path-comparison extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. General ramified-model comparison is requested explicitly, not inferred from coefficient extension.
proofSteps: Apply the nonlinear coordinate-period functor to each crystalline torsor, together with the finite coordinate filtrations.
Use admissible-classification over K⊗R.
Check naturality on coefficient rings; import the Weil restriction adjunction and apply represented-functor naturality to produce the scheme morphism.
acceptance: Nilpotent coefficient maps are retained, and D_n commutes with depth projection.
For K=ℚ_p no Weil restriction is needed; invertibility is not a prerequisite of the finiteness argument.

nodes.title: The local étale path-class map
nodes.statement: For the good-reduction datum of local-albanese, define localEtaleAlbanese_n(x)=[P_n^et(b,x)]∈H¹_f(G_K,U_n^et)(ℚ_p) for x∈𝒳(O_K). The right geometric étale path torsor has continuous G_K-action and its ind-coordinate ring is crystalline by the NC.2 nonlinear good-reduction comparison. The cocycle class is independent of a chosen geometric path used to express it. It is a class in a pointed set, not an element of a group at nonabelian depth. The base point gives the neutral class. The crystalline condition is proved for these geometric path torsors; it is not inferred from unrestricted extension-closure of crystalline representations.
hypotheses: Integral endpoints and good smooth proper compactification with finite étale boundary.
NC.2 nonlinear path comparison and NC.3 represented crystalline torsor interpretation.

For an arbitrary ramified K/ℚ_p, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The cited NC.2 berthelot-ogus and crystalline-path-coordinates nodes cover unramified models; finite-path-comparison extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. General ramified-model comparison is requested explicitly, not inferred from coefficient extension.

Apply the NC.3 torsor-to-cocycle comparison and quotient the full gauge action.
Use NC.2 crystalline path coordinates to place the class in the specified local subfunctor.
acceptance: A change of geometric path changes a cocycle by the gauge action, not by naive addition of a coboundary.
At depth one the map agrees with the rational p-adic Kummer class of x−b for a proper curve.

nodes.title: The global étale path-class map
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, R=O_{F,S}, 𝒳/R a smooth hyperbolic curve with smooth proper compactification and finite étale boundary, and b∈𝒳(R). Fix p and T containing S and every p-adic place, and assume the NC.2 geometric G_F-actions on U_n^et and every permitted path torsor factor continuously through G_{F,T}. For x∈𝒳(R), define globalEtaleAlbanese_n(x)=[P_n^et(b,x)]∈Sel_T(U_n)(ℚ_p), provided every chosen local condition contains the local path class of each permitted global point. In particular at the selected good place v∉S over p use the crystalline condition. Good places outside T have unramified path classes; additional bad-place conditions must be justified, not discarded. In the proper case take D empty, S containing bad reduction places, and 𝒳(R)=X(F) by properness. At b the map is neutral if all selected conditions contain the neutral path class.
hypotheses: Integral global base point and chosen good place v∉S with completion K.

T is finite. At each finite place outside T, inertia acts trivially on U_n^et and on every permitted geometric path torsor, giving actual continuous G_{F,T}-actions. NC.2 etale-galois supplies G_F-actions but does not prove this factorization; the good-integral-model specialization theorem is requested from NC.2.
Every imposed local condition is coefficient-stable and contains the geometric local classes relevant to 𝒳(R); Selmer representability is an additional input when the scheme is used.
proofSteps: Take the geometric path with its continuous G_F-action and use the explicit inertia-triviality/factorization input to descend the group and torsor actions to G_{F,T}. Good-model factorization is a separate supplier theorem, not a consequence of etale-galois alone.
Use NC.3 torsor comparison to form the nonabelian cohomology class.
Verify membership at all imposed local conditions; then factor through the existing Selmer functor.
For a proper curve apply the valuative criterion at the places outside S to identify the global domain.
acceptance: Imposing an arbitrary bad-place condition need not preserve global-point containment.
The claim concerns S-integral points for an open curve and rational points for a proper curve; it does not replace one by the other.

nodes.title: The global Selmer period morphism
nodes.statement: For the NC.3 represented finite-type global Selmer scheme S_n and local crystalline scheme L_n at the chosen good p-adic place K, let loc_n:S_n→L_n be the supplied localization morphism. Define selmerPeriod_n=crystallinePeriodMap_n∘loc_n:S_n→Res_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n as a morphism of ℚ_p-schemes. At K=ℚ_p its target is Q_n. At ℚ_p-points it evaluates localization followed by the crystalline period; its scheme-theoretic image and Zariski closure are taken using the full morphism, not the set of ℚ_p-rational source points. For K≠ℚ_p its base change followed by the Weil-restriction counit gives an auxiliary K-morphism (S_n)_K→Q_n; this is only used with the corresponding K-dimension bound and geometric image closure.
hypotheses: All NC.3 representability and local-condition hypotheses, and crystalline-period hypotheses.
Localization lands in the crystalline scheme at the selected place.
proofSteps: Import localization rather than reconstructing continuous cohomology or the Selmer scheme.
Compose the represented morphisms; at a test algebra the Yoneda map is composition with the same morphism.
Use the imported Weil restriction counit for the auxiliary K-morphism if needed.
acceptance: The composite has a source and target over the same coefficient field.
The construction retains all global local conditions and does not identify Selmer points with rational curve points.

nodes.title: The exact, period-image and closed-image loci
nodes.statement: Put Y=𝒳(O_K), j_n=localAlbanese_n, j_n^et=localEtaleAlbanese_n, and ℓ_n=selmerPeriod_n on ℚ_p-points (interpreted in Q_n(K)). Let Z_n be the reduced Zariski closure of the geometric image of the full scheme morphism ℓ_n in Res_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n; define closedDeRhamLocus_n={y∈Y:j_n(y)∈Z_n(ℚ_p)}. Then crystallineLocus_n⊆deRhamLocus_n⊆closedDeRhamLocus_n. The first inclusion uses the fundamental-diagram; equality requires a separate saturation/injectivity property of D_n. The second inclusion need not be equality: taking the geometric image closure does not promise a ℚ_p-rational Selmer lift. For a K-valued auxiliary morphism use its own geometric image closure and call the resulting enlarged locus by that morphism, not by an unexplained change of scalars. Native set reductions take the supplied maps between actual point carriers, and for the closed locus the supplied point subset Z_n(ℚ_p); computing that subset from the scheme morphism is a separate geometric interface.

nodes.title: Depth projection and change of conditions for the loci
nodes.statement: For m≤n suppose the quotient U_n→U_m induces maps S_n→S_m, L_n→L_m and Q_n→Q_m preserving every chosen local condition and commuting with the local and global period diagrams. Then crystallineLocus_n⊆crystallineLocus_m and deRhamLocus_n⊆deRhamLocus_m; the corresponding closed-image loci are nested because the continuous algebraic quotient maps carry the higher geometric image closure into the lower one. For two systems of conditions on the same global functor, inclusion C_v⊆C′_v at every place gives inclusion of all three loci from the more restrictive to the less restrictive system. At fixed depth, if D_n is injective on local crystalline ℚ_p-points, then crystallineLocus_n=deRhamLocus_n; more generally equality follows if the localization image is saturated under D_n on the local geometric classes. No unconditional equality with the closed-image locus or with the rational point set is asserted.
hypotheses: Represented diagram maps exist and preserve the specified local conditions.
For the last assertion, injectivity or the stated saturation is an additional hypothesis.

In the proper case the first term is the image of X(F). This supplies a global Selmer witness for each integral or rational point. If a locus is finite, so is the global domain, since the field inclusion F→K induces an injective map on points of the F-scheme X. The theorem claims neither the reverse containment nor equality of the intersection with the global set.

nodes.title: Pullback of regular period functions
nodes.statement: For A_n=O(Q_n) and Y=𝒳(O_K), define regularAlbanesePullback_n:A_n→(Y→K) by f↦(y↦f(j_n(y))). It is a K-algebra homomorphism, and iterated-coordinates shows its image consists of the corresponding Coleman functions on ordinary integral discs. The algebra-valued refinement targets the imported Coleman function algebra once its native carrier and the geometric evaluation bridge are available; the function-valued map itself is fully expressible on K-points viewed as K-algebra homomorphisms A_n→K. Disc-density implies that restriction of this map to any nonempty residue disc is injective. If f vanishes on the global Selmer geometric image closure, its pullback vanishes on the de Rham and closed-image loci, and hence on allowed global points.
hypotheses: The period variety is affine and geometrically integral over K; use the geometric K-variant of the image closure if K≠ℚ_p.
Local point evaluation and Coleman membership follow the NC.2/L1 word-path convention.

nodes.title: A regular equation from a small Selmer image
nodes.statement: Let k be a characteristic-zero field, S a finite-type affine k-scheme, Q a geometrically integral affine finite-type k-scheme, and ℓ:S→Q a k-morphism. Let Z be the reduced closed subscheme whose underlying set is the closure of the geometric image of ℓ. If dim S<dim Q, then dim Z≤dim S, Z≠Q, and there exists a nonzero f∈O(Q) vanishing on Z. The same conclusion holds under the weaker hypothesis dim Z<dim Q. Here dimensions are Krull dimensions of schemes, not vector-space ranks of their coordinate rings. Nilpotents of S are retained in ℓ but do not enlarge the topological image; f need only vanish on the reduced closure, not pull back to zero on a nonreduced S. For S empty take Z empty and f=1. At k=ℚ_p, apply this to selmerPeriod_n. For K≠ℚ_p one may apply it instead to the auxiliary K-morphism (S_n)_K→Q_n under dim_{ℚ_p}S_n<dim_K Q_n; merely having dim S_n<dim Res Q_n does not give this conclusion in Q_n.
hypotheses: Finite type is required for the image dimension bound; Q is integral and affine for a nonzero global regular equation.
All dimensions and the image morphism are over the same stated field.
proofSteps: For each irreducible component of the reduced source, use the generic fibre dimension formula to bound the dimension of its image closure.
Take the finite union of component image closures; strict inequality makes it proper.
A proper reduced closed subscheme of an affine integral scheme has a nonzero defining ideal; choose f in that ideal.
For the K-variant use the Weil restriction counit and invariance of source dimension under field extension.
acceptance: For ℓ:A¹→A¹ given by u↦u², dimensions are equal and Z=Q, so the theorem supplies no equation even though many k-points have no lift.
For a constant map into A², a coordinate vanishing at the image point is a possible nonzero f.

nodes.title: Finiteness under discwise nonvanishing
nodes.statement: Let K/ℚ_p be finite and let Y=𝒳(O_K) be the integral tube in a smooth proper good-reduction compactification with finite étale boundary removed. Let j:Y→Q(K) have Coleman-analytic regular-function pullbacks on each ordinary residue disc. If Z⊊Q is a closed subset and some f∈O(Q), f≠0, vanishes on Z and f∘j is not identically zero on each nonempty integral residue disc, then {y∈Y:j(y)∈Z(K)} is finite. In particular the image-defined locus contained in that set is finite. Every disc has K-points parametrized by m_K=πO_K; the pullback on the open geometric disc has a convergent power series, and substituting t=πs produces a nonzero restricted series on the compact closed unit disc O_K. Strassmann then gives finitely many zeros in each disc, and there are finitely many residue discs. The statement supplies finiteness, not an effective uniform bound or equality with global points.
hypotheses: Finite extension K is essential for compactness and a finite residue field; the full C_p-disc is not the domain.
The local functions are analytic on the whole ordinary open geometric residue disc and nonzero on each integral disc.
Only integral discs disjoint from the removed boundary are used; no open punctured-disc compactness assertion is made.
proofSteps: Use the existing good-reduction residue-disc parameterization from L1 and the finiteness of 𝒳(k).
Rescale t=πs: convergence at a real radius strictly between |π| and 1 implies the rescaled coefficients tend to zero.
Use the ED.4 Strassmann theorem on each nonzero rescaled series.
Take a finite union of finite zero sets, then its subset cut out by Z.
acceptance: If f∘j vanishes identically on one disc, that disc may remain wholly in the locus and the criterion does not apply.
An arbitrary nonzero function analytic only on an open disc need not have finitely many zeros throughout that geometric disc.

sources.match: Kim bounds the integral local set by zeros on finitely many residue discs. The rescaling specifies the compact domain needed to apply the imported Strassmann theorem.

nodes.title: Conditional Chabauty–Kim finiteness
nodes.statement: Let X/ℚ be smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic, with integral global base point b and the good models, ramification set and local conditions of global-etale-albanese. Choose p∉S and depth n≥1. Assume the NC.3 global Selmer functor is represented by a finite-type affine scheme S_n and the crystalline comparison gives the morphism ℓ_n:S_n→Q_n at K=ℚ_p. If dim S_n<dim Q_n, then closedDeRhamLocus_n, deRhamLocus_n and crystallineLocus_n are finite, and consequently 𝒳(ℤ[S⁻¹]) is finite. If X is proper, X(ℚ) is finite. One may replace the inequality by a proper geometric image closure together with a nonzero regular annihilator; Kim discwise density supplies the needed nonvanishing. No assertion that a depth satisfying the inequality exists is included: Kim Conjecture 1 and motivic conjectural dimension inputs remain hypotheses, not theorems of NC.4. For a number field F, use finite-annihilator-locus with its explicit K-nonvanishing hypothesis, or the auxiliary K-morphism bound dim S_n<dim_K Q_n; a bound against dim_{ℚ_p}Res Q_n alone is insufficient without stronger Weil-restriction discwise density.
hypotheses: All local conditions contain the allowed global path classes, including bad places.
The nonlinear comparison and representability inputs are supplied; they remain imported plans with their recorded gaps.
The strict dimension inequality is a verified or assumed mathematical input, never silently concluded from the theorem.
proofSteps: Use selmer-annihilator to choose a nonzero regular equation for the geometric Selmer period image closure.
Use residue-disc-density and regular-pullback to obtain a nonzero analytic function on every integral disc.
Apply finite-annihilator-locus and the three locus inclusions.
Use rational-integral-containment and the injective field embedding to deduce global finiteness.
acceptance: For a proper genus-g curve at depth one the target has dimension g; the source dimension is a Selmer dimension, not automatically the Mordell–Weil rank.
The statement applies even when the period map itself is not injective.

nodes.title: The depth-one Albanese and abelian logarithm
nodes.statement: For a proper smooth geometrically connected genus-g curve X/ℚ with b∈X(ℚ) and good reduction at p, use NC.2's abelianization U_1^et=V_pJ and the filtered de Rham identification U_1^dR=H¹_dR(X/ℚ_p)^∨, H_1=Ann(H⁰(X,Ω¹)), Q_1≃Lie(J). With the Lie identification normalized to the endpoint Kummer/Abel–Jacobi comparison, the local crystalline path class is κ_p(AJ_b(x)) and the identified de Rham period is log_J(AJ_b(x)). Pairing with ω∈H⁰(X,Ω¹) gives the single Coleman integral ∫_b^xω. Fix the convention explicitly: in NC.2's universal connection d−∑T_iω_i the forward Frobenius path has coefficient +I_i; our torsor ratio has representative I⁻¹γ, so its raw first-level coordinate is γ_i−I_i. The Lie comparison sends the raw quotient coordinate with the compensating sign to the usual logarithm; it does not identify +I_i with that raw torsor ratio. This sign normalization leaves linear-subspace loci unchanged. For an open curve the generalized Jacobian/boundary contribution is a separate input, and is not identified with the proper Jacobian in this node.
hypotheses: Proper curve and NC.2's de Rham H¹/Hodge–Abel–Jacobi bridge; good-reduction rational Tate-module comparison.
Use the same path direction b→x and the displayed ratio convention in every realization.
proofSteps: Import the NC.2 depth-one group and cohomology bridge; do not reconstruct J, the Tate module or the Hodge exact sequence.
Use the NC.3 depth-one comparison for the actual Kummer class.
Use ED.4’s abelian logarithm and Coleman/abelian integral comparison, transporting the raw coordinate sign through the normalized Lie identification.
acceptance: Depth one here is Kim U_2, and Q_1 has dimension g; depth zero is trivial.
For x=b every pairing is zero; for a differential the derivative of the paired period is ω, with the above sign normalization.
The open-curve target includes puncture directions and needs the generalized Jacobian; deleting them would change the definition.

nodes.title: The precise classical Chabauty comparison
nodes.statement: In depth-one-period's proper setting, let W_S⊆Lie(J)(ℚ_p) be the image of the linear global Selmer space under the normalized logarithmic period map, and W_MW=span_{ℚ_p}{log_J(P):P∈J(ℚ)}. The de Rham image locus at depth one is {x∈X(ℚ_p):log_J(AJ_b(x))∈W_S}, equivalently the common zero set of ∫_b^xω for all linear forms ω∈Ann(W_S). The image is already a closed linear subspace, so its period-image and geometric-closed-image loci coincide in this linear setting. For the usual local conditions the Mordell–Weil Kummer map lies in the Selmer space, giving W_MW⊆W_S; if additional conditions are imposed, this containment must be an explicit hypothesis. The classical common-annihilator Chabauty locus is obtained by replacing W_S with W_MW, and is a subset of the Selmer locus under that containment. If W_S=W_MW, the two loci agree. A rank bound rank J(ℚ)<g gives dim W_MW<g and classical finiteness by the imported ED.4 theory, but gives finiteness of the full depth-one Selmer locus only with dim W_S<g (e.g. W_S=W_MW). No vanishing of a Tate–Shafarevich contribution or equality Selmer=Mordell–Weil is assumed without a stated extra input. The common-annihilator locus is logarithmically saturated; it is not asserted equal to AJ_b⁻¹ of the literal topological closure of J(ℚ).
hypotheses: All depth-one-period hypotheses; the represented depth-one Selmer space and period map are linear over ℚ_p.
Containment of the whole Mordell–Weil Kummer image is needed when comparing its classical locus with a refined Selmer locus.
Equality of the two period subspaces is a separate hypothesis.
proofSteps: Import the linear rational Tate-module Selmer and Kummer comparison from NC.3.
Identify the first de Rham map with the logarithm by depth-one-period.
Use the baseline double-annihilator identity to express membership in W_S by all annihilating linear forms.
Use ED.4 annihilating differentials and residue-disc zero bounds for classical finiteness; retain the separate Selmer dimension input.
acceptance: If W_S=Lie(J) and W_MW is proper, the full Selmer locus is X(ℚ_p) while the classical locus can be finite.
For W=0 the period-image locus is the zero logarithm fibre; for W=Lie(J) it is the whole local curve.
The annihilator formulation preserves constants of integration through the same global base point b.
